fields.topology_type: Multi-drop 2-pin DDR bus (SoundWire_Clock + SoundWire_Data Lane 0) with optional Data Lanes 1..7 for higher aggregate bandwidth. Single Master per bus; up to 11 Slave Devices; optional Monitor (test equipment) snooping and occasionally taking over via BREQ/BREL.

supported_topologies.name: AP Direct-Attach
supported_topologies.description: Application Processor Master drives multiple ADC / DAC Slaves directly on a single Clock + Data tree. Webinar slide 'Example topologies' top-left example.

supported_topologies.name: Bridges, Inter-Chip Link
supported_topologies.description: Application Processor Master ↔ Bridge Slave (Master on the other side) ↔ downstream ADC/DAC Slaves; allows reach extension to BT FM Radio chip. Webinar slide 'Example topologies' bottom-left.

supported_topologies.name: Inter-Chip Link with Multi-Lane Support
supported_topologies.description: Application Processor Master ↔ Audio Codec Slave with Data[0]..Data[2] separate Data lanes; BT FM Radio + DSP on additional lanes. Webinar slide 'Example topologies' right.

supported_topologies.name: Functional Partitioning
supported_topologies.description: Application Processor with two Master instances driving disjoint Slave groups (e.g. one Master for input ADCs, one for output DACs). Webinar slide 'Example topologies (2)' left.

supported_topologies.name: Routing / Use-Case Partitioning
supported_topologies.description: Independent Master pairs each owning a separate Clock + Data tree for different audio use cases. Webinar slide 'Example topologies (2)' right.

supported_topologies.name: Shared PHY
supported_topologies.description: Module-level integration where pins are shared — Master Digital Interface plus Slave Digital Interfaces feed a single shared PHY block providing external Clock/Data pads. Webinar slide 'Shared and virtual PHY' left.

supported_topologies.name: Virtual PHY
supported_topologies.description: Pins are NOT visible externally — SoundWire used inside a module; an OR-gate / clock-doubler virtual PHY provides the bus to internal digital interfaces. Webinar slide 'Shared and virtual PHY' right.

supported_topologies.name: Monitor-Augmented Bus
supported_topologies.description: Any of the above plus a Monitor (test equipment) that snoops the bus and may temporarily take over via BREQ/BREL arbitration.

responsibilities: Provides Clock and sync pattern on Data line.
Handles all bus management, bit allocation, Frame Shape, ClockStop.
Drives Control Word in Col 0 Rows 0..47 of every Frame.
Sends PING, READ, WRITE, BRA/BTP, ClockStopNow commands.
Performs enumeration of Slaves by reading SCP_Device0..5 (48-bit value) and assigning Device Numbers 1..11.
Performs synchronized bank switch (SCP_FrameCtrl0/1) for safe reconfiguration.
Drives Parity bit (or sets NAK on parity error while Monitor owns bus).
Configures per-Port HStart, HStop, SampleInterval, BlockOffset, SubBlockOffset.
Manages Wake-from-ClockStop permissions per-Slave.
Typically audio peripheral (microphone, codec, smart amplifier, smart speaker).
1..11 Slaves connected to Master over multi-drop bus.
Verify Static + Dynamic sync for 16 consecutive frames before declaring Attached.
Drive own three-state status (Not Attached / Attached / Alert) in PING frames.
Respond ACK / NAK / Command_Ignored to READ / WRITE commands.
Drive Read Data payload in next Frame after READ.
Drive audio payload in assigned Source-Port BitSlots; receive payload in assigned Sink-Port BitSlots.
Maintain hardware-mandatory 48-bit enumeration value in SCP_Device0..5.
Ability to signal Interrupt condition via PREQ / Alert status / DPst_IntStat.
Ability to wake-up the system (subject to Master's permission bitmap).
Never drive SoundWire_Clock.
Test equipment, in snooping/analyzer mode most of the time.
Can temporarily take over the bus via BREQ/BREL arbitration.
Issue PING / READ / WRITE commands when owning the Command Word.
If Monitor loses sync, command will default to PING with BREQ cleared and Master will reclaim ownership.
Master always drives static and dynamic sync bits and may set NAK on parity error even when Monitor owns the Command Word.
Acts as Slave on the upstream bus and as Master on a downstream secondary bus.
Used for reach extension and topology hierarchy.

fields.interconnect_role: There is no central protocol-layer interconnect — the bus is a flat multi-drop shared medium with one Clock + one (or more) Data lanes. Bridge Slaves can extend reach by acting as Master of a downstream bus. From the application firmware perspective the bus behaves as a single shared 2-pin link with embedded command and data carrying both audio and control.

ordering_guarantees.within_a_frame: Bits are transmitted serially in column-major-within-row bitstream order across the 2-D Frame; the Control Word is always at Col 0 Rows 0..47.
ordering_guarantees.across_frames: Each Read/Write command has a 1-frame round-trip (response in next Frame's Command Status / Read Data field).
ordering_guarantees.across_ports: Stream aggregation requires same SampleInterval on all participating Ports + common bank-switch event; 'smart' bit allocation places port BitSlots adjacently with no spacing.
ordering_guarantees.across_buses: No fairness guarantee across multiple SoundWire buses; they are independent. SSP can be used to maintain alignment between multiple links with different frame rates.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: Not a memory bus. SoundWire's 16-bit register address space is per-Slave: normative 0x0000-0x0FFF, device-class reserved 0x1000-0x17FF, implementation-defined 0x2000-0xFFFF, paged implementation 0x10000-0x3FFFFFFF.

slave_classification.audio_input_slave: Microphone / ADC peripheral driving Source Ports.
slave_classification.audio_output_slave: Speaker / DAC / amplifier peripheral receiving Sink Ports.
slave_classification.codec_slave: Combined ADC + DAC + audio DSP; mix of Source and Sink Ports.
slave_classification.smart_amplifier: Class-D output stage with I/V sensing feedback Source Port + audio input Sink Port.
slave_classification.bt_fm_radio: Bluetooth / FM Radio with audio streams (typically two Data lanes Data[0], Data[1]).
slave_classification.dsp_slave: Audio DSP performing post-processing; both Source and Sink Ports.
slave_classification.bridge_slave: Slave that further routes to a downstream sub-bus.
slave_classification.monitor: Test equipment for development / debug / certification.
slave_classification.wakeable_slave: Slave that may initiate wake-up from ClockStop; subject to Master's wake-permission bitmap.
slave_classification.interrupt_capable: Every Slave can raise interrupts; reflected as Alert status in PING + SCP_IntStat_* / DPst_IntStat registers.

addressing_topology.device_0: Reserved for un-enumerated Slaves; used during enumeration handshake.
addressing_topology.group_addresses: Address one configured group of Slaves; group membership is held in Slave registers.
addressing_topology.broadcast_15: Addresses all Slaves on the bus.

bus_management_overview.monitor_ownership: Optional Monitor may own the Command Word transiently via BREQ=1 AND BREL=1; Master can reclaim by clearing BREL.
bus_management_overview.bank_switch: Atomic synchronized reconfiguration via SCP_FrameCtrl0/1 toggle at the next SSP tick.
bus_management_overview.clockstop_modes: Mode 0 mandatory (context retained); Mode 1 optional (context may be lost).
bus_management_overview.wake_permission: Master programs which Slaves are allowed to wake the bus.
bus_management_overview.ssp_safe_reconfig: SSP tick (≥ once every 100 ms) defines safe time positions for bus reconfiguration.
